question:
If in ΔABC, AB = AC and ∠ACD = 125°, then ∠BAC is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/959a88bb9d043b08e86eca803e304670c2a098183aaa7948cf04d493eb9ea48f.png]
solution:
**Given:**

A triangle ABC , AB = AC and angleACD = 125^circ 

**Concept used:**

If two sides are equal, then angles opposite to their sides are also equal 

Sum of the angles in a triangle is 180^circ 

If a side of a triangle is produced , the exterior angle so formed is equal to the 

sum of the two interior opposite angles 

**Calculation:**

** ** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a203cd3818bf504b2b5e300da9aebe06461e70b5a8c0c206b32beb32d0747a78.png] 

Here, we have a triangle triangleABC in which AB = AC 

So, angles angleACB = angleABC = x(let us say) ( angles opposite to the equal sides)

As, we know that 

Sum of the angles in a triangle = 180^circ 

⇒ angleACB + angleABC + angleBAC = 180 

⇒ x + x + angleBAC = 180 

⇒ angleBAC = 180 -2x 

As,angleACD = exterior angle of a triangle ABC 

⇒ angleACD = angleBAC + angleACB

⇒ 125 = 180 - 2x + x 

⇒ x = 55^circ

angleBAC = 180 - 2x = 180 - ( 2 × 55) 

⇒ 180 - 110 = 70^circ

**Hence, the value of angle BAC is 70^circ****.**
